title: Text the compiler cannot read
plain: Text the compiler cannot read
summary: A character that begins nothing the language has, or a string, comment or splice that never closes. The file is not read past it.
description: A character that begins nothing the language has, or a string, comment or splice that never closes. The file is not read past it.
printed:
error[E001]: Unterminated string literal
 --> src/App.wf:2:13
  |
2 |     Heading("Hello).h1
  |             ^
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E001
fix:
Close the string, comment or splice the message names. A
character that begins nothing (`|` alone, a stray `@`) is usually a typo
for the one beside it on the keyboard.

title: A syntax error
plain: A syntax error
summary: The text reads, but not as the language: a missing brace, a stray word, an argument list that does not close. The message names what was expected and what was found.
description: The text reads, but not as the language: a missing brace, a stray word, an argument list that does not close. The message names what was expected and…
printed:
error[E002]: Expected `,` between arguments, got `Text`
 --> src/App.wf:3:14
  |
3 |     Text("a" Text("b")
  |              ^^^^
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E002
fix:
The message names what was expected and what was found, at the
place the parser stopped. One file can report several: after an error the
parser picks up again at the next declaration.

title: Indentation that lines up with no block
plain: Indentation that lines up with no block
summary: In a `.wfx` file a line opens a block by being followed by a deeper one, and closes blocks by coming back out. A line that comes back to an indentation no enclosing block has is ambiguous.
description: In a `.wfx` file a line opens a block by being followed by a deeper one, and closes blocks by coming back out. A line that comes back to an…
why:
In a `.wfx` file, a line that comes back out to an indentation no enclosing
block has:

```text
page Home(path: "/")
    Row
        Text("a")
      Text("b")
```
fix: Line the line up with the block it belongs to.

title: A file in the WebFluent 2 grammar
plain: A file in the WebFluent 2 grammar
summary: WebFluent 3 reads one grammar. `wf migrate` rewrites a WebFluent 2 project in place.
description: WebFluent 3 reads one grammar. `wf migrate` rewrites a WebFluent 2 project in place.
printed:
error[E004]: `Page` is a WebFluent 2 declaration; this is WebFluent 3
 --> src/App.wf:1:1
  |
1 | Page Home (path: "/") {
  | ^^^^
  = help: Run `wf migrate` to convert the project to the current grammar
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E004
fix: Run `wf migrate` once; it rewrites the project in place.

title: A file the formatter will not change
plain: A file the formatter will not change
summary: `wf fmt` holds its result to the file's tokens; when formatting would change what a file says, it leaves the file alone and says so.
description: `wf fmt` holds its result to the file's tokens; when formatting would change what a file says, it leaves the file alone and says so.
why:
`wf fmt` checks that its result has the same tokens as the file. When it
would not — something only the formatter's reading of the file would
change — the file is left as it is and named.
fix:
format the lines it
names by hand; please report the file, since it is a bug in `wf fmt`.

plain: A component nothing declares
summary: An element, a `layout:` or a part names a component that no `component` declares and no built-in has. Often a misspelling.
description: An element, a `layout:` or a part names a component that no `component` declares and no built-in has. Often a misspelling.
printed:
error[E101]: unknown component `Buton`: no `component Buton` is declared
 --> src/App.wf:3:5

3 |     Buton("Save")
  |     ^^^^^
  = help: did you mean `Button`? Or declare `component Buton { … }`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E101
fix: Check the spelling, or declare it with `component Buton { … }`.

title: A name declared twice
plain: A name declared twice
summary: Two declarations with one name in one scope: two stores, two constants, a state and a derived of one name. It compiled to a script the browser refused, or let the second quietly replace the first.
description: Two declarations with one name in one scope: two stores, two constants, a state and a derived of one name. It compiled to a script the browser…
printed:
error[E102]: `count` is declared twice: as a state at line 2, and as a `derived` here
 --> src/App.wf:3:5
  |
3 |     derived count = 1
  |     ^^^^^^^
  = help: A name means one thing — rename one of the two `count`s
  = note: `count` is first declared here at src/App.wf:2:5
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E102
fix:
Rename one of the two. The finding points at the second and names
where the first is.

title: A flag, case, part, event or slot the component does not have
plain: A flag, case, part, event or slot the component does not have
summary: What a component takes comes from one registry for the built-ins and from the declaration for your own; a word that resolves to nothing there does nothing on screen, so it is refused.
description: What a component takes comes from one registry for the built-ins and from the declaration for your own; a word that resolves to nothing there does…
printed:
error[E103]: Button has no flag or enum case `huge`
 --> src/App.wf:3:19
  |
3 |     Button("Save").huge
  |                   ^^^^^
  = help: Its flags are .bounce, .button, .collapse, .danger, .disabled, .dropInside, .expand, .fadeIn, .fadeOut, .fast, .full, .info, .lg, .md, .normal, .outlined, .pill, .primary, .pulse, .reset, .rounded, .scaleIn, .scaleOut, .secondary, .shake, .slideDown, .slideLeft, .slideRight, .slideUp, .slow, .sm, .spin, .submit, .success, .trapFocus, .warning
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E103
fix:
Use one the message lists — it names every flag, case, event or
slot the component takes.

title: A layout with nowhere to put the page
plain: A layout with nowhere to put the page
summary: A page's `layout:` is a component the page is placed in, at its default slot. A component that declares no `slot` has nowhere to put it.
description: A page's `layout:` is a component the page is placed in, at its default slot. A component that declares no `slot` has nowhere to put it.
printed:
error[E104]: `Shell` declares no default slot, so the page has nowhere to go
 --> src/App.wf:2:57
  |
2 | page P(path: "/", title: "T", description: "D", layout: Shell) {
  |                                                         ^^^^^
  = help: Add `slot` to the component and place `children` where the page belongs
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E104
fix:
Add `slot` to the component and place `children` where the page
belongs.

title: A statement a render block cannot hold
plain: A statement a render block cannot hold
summary: A page's or component's body draws; an assignment or a call that does something belongs in a handler, an `action` or an `effect`.
description: A page's or component's body draws; an assignment or a call that does something belongs in a handler, an `action` or an `effect`.
printed:
error[E105]: `n` is not an element or a statement a render block can hold
 --> src/App.wf:4:5
  |
4 |     n = n + 1
  |     ^
  = help: Code that does something goes in `on click { … }`, an `action` or an `effect`; an element's name is capitalised
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E105
fix: Put it in `on click { }`, an `action` or an `effect`.

title: Script or a whole style in an attribute
plain: Script or a whole style in an attribute
summary: `onclick:` and the other `on*` attributes are script in a string, which the content security policy refuses and nothing checks. A handler is `on click { … }`. `style:` is a value written as the element's whole inline style; a style is a `style { }` block, one property at a time.
description: `onclick:` and the other `on*` attributes are script in a string, which the content security policy refuses and nothing checks. A handler is `on…
printed:
error[E106]: `onclick` on Button would put script in an attribute
 --> src/App.wf:3:20
  |
3 |     Button("Save", onclick: "save()")
  |                    ^^^^^^^
  = help: Write the handler instead: `Button(…) { on click { … } }`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E106
fix:
`Button("Save") { on click { save() } }`.

`style:` is refused the same way: it would write a value as the
element's whole `style=` attribute, which a value from data can turn
into a box over the whole page or a request to anywhere. A style is a
`style { }` block, one property at a time, where a value that reads
state sets that one property and nothing else.

```wf expect=E106
page P(path: "/", title: "T", description: "D") {
    state look = "color: red"
    Heading("Note").h1
    Text("Hi", style: look)
}
```

```text
error[E106]: `style:` on Text would write a value as the element's whole inline style
 --> src/App.wf:4:16
  |
4 |     Text("Hi", style: look)
  |                ^^^^^
  = help: Write a style block instead: `Text(…) { style { color: {tone} } }`, one property at a time
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E106
```

**Fix:** `Text("Hi") { style { color: {tone} } }`.

title: A URL a browser would run
plain: A URL a browser would run
summary: `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `blob:` and `file:` URLs run or load something the page did not write. A link takes `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `tel`, `sms`, `ftp` or a relative URL. In `head { }`, a `script(src:)` or a refresh whose address a value chooses is refused the same way.
description: `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `blob:` and `file:` URLs run or load something the page did not write. A link takes `http`, `https`, `mailto`,…
printed:
error[E107]: `to` on Link names the `javascript` scheme, which a browser runs
 --> src/App.wf:3:16
  |
3 |     Link("Go", to: "javascript:alert(1)")
  |                ^^
  = help: A URL here may be relative, or name http, https, mailto, tel, sms or ftp
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E107
fix:
A relative URL, or `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `tel`, `sms`,
`ftp`.

A page's `head { }` is held to the same rule, and more: a
`script(src:)` must be written out, since whoever controls a value it
reads would choose the script the page runs; a `meta(http-equiv:
"refresh")` whose address comes from a value is an open redirect, and
an `http-equiv` a value chooses could become one.

```wf expect=E107
page P(path: "/", title: "T", description: "D") {
    head { script(src: query.lib) }
    Heading("Home").h1
}
```

```text
error[E107]: `head { script(src: …) }` loads a script a value chooses: whoever controls the value runs code as this site
 --> src/App.wf:2:12
  |
2 |     head { script(src: query.lib) }
  |            ^^^^^^
  = help: Write the address out — `script(src: "/analytics.js")` — and keep what varies in the script's own data
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E107
```

**Fix:** `head { script(src: "/analytics.js") }`; send a reader on with
`navigate(…)`, which keeps to the site's routes.

title: An `env` name that is not public
plain: An env name that is not public
summary: Whatever a page reads from `env` is in the bundle, where anyone can read it. A name a page reads must begin `PUBLIC_` or be listed in `public_env`.
description: Whatever a page reads from `env` is in the bundle, where anyone can read it. A name a page reads must begin `PUBLIC_` or be listed in `public_env`.
why:
`env.STRIPE_SECRET` read in a page: `env.STRIPE_SECRET is not public, and a
page reads what is in the bundle`.
fix:
rename it `PUBLIC_…` or list it
in `public_env` — only if anyone may read it ([chapter
30](../recipes/environments.md)).

title: An element this output cannot draw
plain: An element this output cannot draw
summary: A PDF or a slide deck has no buttons, inputs, handlers or routes; an interactive element in one would be drawn as nothing.
description: A PDF or a slide deck has no buttons, inputs, handlers or routes; an interactive element in one would be drawn as nothing.
why:
A `Button`, an `Input`, a handler or a `Router` in a project whose
`output_type` is `pdf` or `slides`. Paper has no controls (`Button`,
`Input`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `Radio`, `Switch`, `Slider`, `DatePicker`,
`FileUpload`, `Textarea`, `Form`, `IconButton`, `ButtonGroup`, `Dropdown`), no navigation
(`Router`, `Navbar`, `Sidebar`, `Tabs`, `Menu`), no overlays (`Modal`,
`Dialog`, `Popover`, `Toast`, `Tooltip`), no media that plays (`Video`,
`Audio`, `Carousel`), no other page inside it (`Frame`) and nothing a
script draws (`Host`, `Element`, `Portal`).
fix:
draw it as text, or build the
page as a site.

title: A project script that cannot be a plain script
plain: A project script that cannot be a plain script
summary: A `.js` file under `src/` is linked as a plain browser script: one with `import` or `export`, one a file in `public/` would replace, or one whose names clash with the program's, cannot be.
description: A `.js` file under `src/` is linked as a plain browser script: one with `import` or `export`, one a file in `public/` would replace, or one whose…
why:
A `.js` file under `src/` with an `import` or `export`, one a file in
`public/` at the same address would replace, or one declaring a name the
program, the language or the browser already has.
fix:
take off the
`import`/`export` (a top-level `function` is global as it is), keep one of
the two files, or rename the clashing name.

title: A setting that cannot work
plain: A setting that cannot work
summary: A value in `webfluent.app.json` that names something that does not exist or asks for something the build cannot do.
description: A value in `webfluent.app.json` that names something that does not exist or asks for something the build cannot do.
why:
A `meta.scripts` module with no `as`, a `build.elements` naming a component
that does not exist, an `offline.fallback` no page has, an `openapi.json`
that is not there.
fix: what the message says; it names the setting.

title: A setting nothing reads
plain: A setting nothing reads
summary: A key in `webfluent.app.json` that is not a setting. Usually a misspelling, so the setting it meant keeps its default.
description: A key in `webfluent.app.json` that is not a setting. Usually a misspelling, so the setting it meant keeps its default.
why:
Warning. A key in `webfluent.app.json` that is not a setting, with the
nearest one that is: `` `build.minfy` is not a setting, and nothing reads it
— did you mean `minify`? ``
fix: correct the key.

title: An argument that cannot be positional
plain: An argument that cannot be positional
summary: Only the first argument of a call may be written without its name, and only when the component declares a positional prop (`_ name`). Name the others.
description: Only the first argument of a call may be written without its name, and only when the component declares a positional prop (`_ name`). Name the others.
printed:
error[E113]: Only the first argument may be positional
 --> src/App.wf:4:20
  |
4 |     Card("Laptop", 999)
  |                    ^^^
  = help: Name the others: `Button("Save", tone: .primary)`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E113
fix: Name the others: `Card("Laptop", price: 999)`.

title: `emit` outside a component
plain: emit outside a component
summary: An event belongs to a component, which declares it and fires it with `emit`; a page has none.
description: An event belongs to a component, which declares it and fires it with `emit`; a page has none.
printed:
error[E114]: `emit` fires a component's event; a page has none
 --> src/App.wf:3:33
  |
3 |     Button("Save") { on click { emit saved() } }
  |                                 ^^^^
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E114
fix:
Fire the event from the component that declares it; a page calls
an action instead.

title: A project script the compiler could not read
plain: A project script the compiler could not read
summary: The file is still linked and may run fine in a browser, but the compiler could not read what it declares, so its names are not in scope for the program.
description: The file is still linked and may run fine in a browser, but the compiler could not read what it declares, so its names are not in scope for the program.
why:
Warning. A `.js` file under `src/` the compiler's scanner could not read —
a string that never closes, say. The file is still linked, but its names
are not in scope for the program.
fix:
what the message says, at the
line it names.

title: A tag that cannot be a custom element's
plain: A tag that cannot be a custom element's
summary: `Element` names a custom element by its tag, first and as a string: lower case, with a hyphen (`"stripe-pricing-table"`).
description: `Element` names a custom element by its tag, first and as a string: lower case, with a hyphen (`"stripe-pricing-table"`).
printed:
error[E116]: `pricingtable` is not a custom element's tag
 --> src/App.wf:3:5
  |
3 |     Element("pricingtable")
  |     ^^^^^^^
  = help: A custom element's tag is lower case with a hyphen: `Element("stripe-pricing-table", …)`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E116
fix:
A custom element's tag is lower case with a hyphen:
`Element("pricing-table")`.

title: A key combination no keyboard sends
plain: A key combination no keyboard sends
summary: `on key(…)` names modifiers (`ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, `meta`) and one key; a modifier it does not know, no key, or a key no keyboard has would never match.
description: `on key(…)` names modifiers (`ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, `meta`) and one key; a modifier it does not know, no key, or a key no keyboard has would never match.
printed:
error[E117]: `on key("ctrl+shfit+k")` names `shfit`, which is not a modifier
 --> src/App.wf:2:12
  |
2 |     on key("ctrl+shfit+k") { log("search") }
  |            ^
  = help: Modifiers `mod` (⌘ on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere), `ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, `meta` (`cmd`), then one key: a letter, a digit, or a name like `Enter`, `Escape`, `ArrowDown`, `Tab`, `F2`; a chord is its steps with a space between, `mod+k mod+s`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E117
fix:
Modifiers `ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, `meta` (or `cmd`), then one key:
a letter, a digit, or a name — `Enter`, `Escape`, `ArrowDown`, `Tab`, `F2`.

title: A name the language already has
plain: A name the language already has
summary: A name the language gives a meaning cannot be a program's own — not a `state`, `derived`, `persist` or `let`, a prop, a route or action parameter, a loop item, a lambda's parameter, a binding of `if let`, `match` or a slot, nor a top-level `const`, `data`, `image`, store or `api`. They are `env`, the build's settings; `params`, the route's; `locale` and `dir`, the reader's language; the values the browser keeps current, `now`, `viewport`, `query`, `hash`, `theme`, `network` and `update`; the language's functions (`t`, `format`, `ago`, `log`, `navigate`, `fetch`, `uuid`, `sanitize`, `every`, `after`, …); the words a statement is written with (`state`, `action`, `let`, `if`, `show`, `match`, `style`, `on`, …); and, at the top level, the runtime's `WF`. Declared, one would hide what the language means by it for as far as its scope reaches. The names a handler brings (`event`, `e`, `value`, `key`) and the browser's globals are a program's to use.
description: A name the language gives a meaning cannot be a program's own — not a `state`, `derived`, `persist` or `let`, a prop, a route or action parameter, a…
printed:
error[E118]: `env` is a name the language already has: the build's settings, read as `env.PUBLIC_API`
 --> src/App.wf:2:5
  |
2 |     state env = "staging"
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Name it something of your own — `target` or `stage`: inside its scope every `env` would mean this, and the language's would have no name
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/E118
why:
A name the language gives a meaning is not a program's to declare — not as
a `state`, `derived`, `persist` or `let`, a prop, a route or action
parameter, a loop item, a lambda's parameter, a binding of `if let`, `match`
or a slot, nor a top-level `const`, `data`, `image`, store or `api`.
Declared, it would hide what the language means by it for as far as its
scope reaches: a `state env` hid the build's settings in its page, and a
loop's `t` hid the translation function inside the loop. The names are:

- `env`, the build's settings; `params`, the route's; `locale` and `dir`,
  the reader's language;
- the values the browser keeps current: `now`, `viewport`, `query`, `hash`,
  `theme`, `network`, `update`;
- the language's functions: `t`, `format`, `ago`, `log`, `navigate`,
  `fetch`, `uuid`, `sanitize`, `setLocale`, `setTheme`, `optimistic`,
  `beacon`, `animate`, `replayAnimation`, `every`, `after`, `ws`, `sse`,
  `broadcast`, `rtc`;
- the words a statement is written with: `state`, `persist`, `derived`,
  `effect`, `action`, `use`, `resource`, `validate`, `socket`, `stream`,
  `channel`, `peer`, `head`, `slot`, `part`, `if`, `else`, `for`, `in`, `by`,
  `show`, `match`, `children`, `emit`, `sequence`, `on`, `style`,
  `transition`, `let`, `return`, `await`, `try`, `catch`;
- at the top level, `WF`, the runtime the compiled pages call;
- in a store, the names every JavaScript object has — `valueOf`,
  `toString`, `constructor`, `hasOwnProperty`, `isPrototypeOf`,
  `propertyIsEnumerable`, `toLocaleString`, `__proto__` and its
  `__define…`/`__lookup…` kin: a store is an object whose members are its
  own, and a `valueOf` member replaced the one JavaScript calls itself, so
  the page threw as soon as it was drawn;
- and, as a prop, `__proto__`, which in the object a call passes sets its
  prototype instead (a prop named `toString` or `valueOf` is fine).

The names a handler brings with it — `event`, `e`, `value`, `key` — and the
browser's globals (`window`, `history`, …) are a program's to use, and so is
any name as a field, a map key or an enum case: `type Box { env: String }`
and `.env` are fine.
fix:
Name it something of your own — `state target = "staging"` — and
its reads with it. The message suggests one where there is a usual choice:
`target` or `stage` for `env`, `search` for `query`, `scheme` for `theme`,
`item` or a word for what it holds for `t`.

title: The compiler wrote JavaScript a browser would refuse
plain: The compiler wrote JavaScript a browser would refuse
summary: The build reads back every script it writes, and this one would not run. It is a bug in WebFluent, not in the program; please report it with the source that produced it.
description: The build reads back every script it writes, and this one would not run. It is a bug in WebFluent, not in the program; please report it with the…
why:
The build reads back every script it writes; this one would not run. It is
a bug in WebFluent, not in your program.
fix:
please report it, with
the source that produced it.

title: Output its own security policy refuses
plain: Output its own security policy refuses
summary: The build holds every page to the content security policy it ships beside it — as it wrote the page, and as the page's own `head { }` tags would add to it; something there would be blocked.
description: The build holds every page to the content security policy it ships beside it — as it wrote the page, and as the page's own `head { }` tags would add…
why:
The build holds every page it writes to the content security policy it
ships beside it; something on this page — an inline script, a `style=`, a
script from an origin the policy never named — would be blocked. A page's
own `head { script(src: …) }` or `head { link(rel: "stylesheet", href: …) }`
is held to it too, where it is written: the tag is added on the live page,
and the browser would refuse it there without a word.
fix:
what the
message says; a library's origin goes in `meta.scripts`, a stylesheet's in
`meta.stylesheets`.

title: A hidden direction control in the source
plain: A hidden direction control in the source
summary: An embedding, override or isolate control (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) is invisible and reorders what follows it, so the code a reader sees is not the code that runs (Trojan Source).
description: An embedding, override or isolate control (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) is invisible and reorders what follows it, so the code a reader sees is not…
why:
Warning. An embedding, override or isolate control — U+202A to U+202E,
U+2066 to U+2069 — is invisible, and it reorders what follows it: a
comment that seems to close, or a string that seems to hold one word, can
hide code that runs (Trojan Source, CVE-2021-42574). The editor draws each
as a mark; the check names each by its line, its column and its Unicode
name.
fix:
remove it. Arabic beside Latin needs no control: each run
takes the direction of its own letters.

Names may be written in Arabic, or any script: a name starts with a letter
and goes on with letters, digits, `_` and the marks of its letters, as
UAX #31 says (`state عددٌ = 3`), and is one name however its letters were
typed — أ precomposed or ا with a combining hamza (NFC).

title: Something nests too deeply
plain: Something nests too deeply
summary: Brackets, blocks, components that place each other, or the links of one chain (`a.b.c`, `1 + 2 + 3`) nest more than 100 levels deep, which no pass of the compiler follows.
description: Brackets, blocks, components that place each other, or the links of one chain (`a.b.c`, `1 + 2 + 3`) nest more than 100 levels deep, which no pass of…
why:
Error. Brackets inside brackets, blocks inside blocks, a splice inside a
string inside a splice, the links of one chain (`a.b.c`, `1 + 2 + 3`,
each link nesting the value one level deeper) and, in a template,
components that place one another — counted together, more than 100
levels deep. The parser, the checker and the template engine each stop
there and say so, where each would otherwise run out of stack. The
deepest program of this guide, the examples and the site nests 15 levels.
fix:
name a part of it — a `let` in an action, a `derived` value, a
component — and use the name. A component that places itself stops when
its data does; one whose data does not end is this error too.

title: A render that would do too much
plain: A render that would do too much
summary: A template's render would draw more elements and loop items, work out more, or write more markup than one render may: nested loops over vast ranges or data, or an expression that makes more than one evaluation may.
description: A template's render would draw more elements and loop items, work out more, or write more markup than one render may: nested loops over vast ranges…
why:
Error, from the template engine (`wf render`, `Template::render_*`). One
render may take ten million steps — an element drawn, a loop item, a unit
of working a value out — and write 256 MB of markup, and one expression
may make about half a million list items or 32 MB of text. A render past
any of them stops and says where, instead of growing until the server
runs out of memory: two nested `for` loops over ranges of a billion, a
loop over the data inside a loop over the data that is too large, or
`(1..=1000000).map(i => 1..=1000000)`. A build that meets such an
expression at build time leaves it to the page, as it does any value it
cannot work out.
fix:
draw less — page the data before it reaches the
template, or work the value out on the server and hand it over.

title: A value of the wrong type
plain: A value of the wrong type
summary: A value given to a prop, a state, a field, a parameter or an assignment that is not of the type it is declared to hold.
description: A value given to a prop, a state, a field, a parameter or an assignment that is not of the type it is declared to hold.
printed:
error[T01]: `count` is `String`, but `Number` is wanted
 --> src/App.wf:4:34
  |
4 |     Button("Reset") { on click { count = "zero" } }
  |                                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Convert it: `Number(value)`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T01
fix:
Give the state a value of its type, or convert: `Number(text)`, `"{n}"`. If the state really holds either, declare it `Any`.

A number a built-in cannot be given is one too: a `Carousel(interval:)`
outside 1 to 2147483647 milliseconds (`-5000` used to become a 0 ms
autoplay), a `Column(span:)` that is not a whole number from 1 to 12.

```wf expect=T01
page P(path: "/", title: "T", description: "D") {
    Heading("Grid").h1
    Row { Column(span: 13) { Text("Wide") } }
}
```

```text
error[T01]: `span` of Column is 13, but a whole number of the 12 columns, from 1 to 12, is wanted
 --> src/App.wf:3:11
  |
3 |     Row { Column(span: 13) { Text("Wide") } }
  |           ^^^^^^
  = help: `span: 6` is half the row
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T01
```

title: A value that may be null, read as if it were not
plain: A value that may be null, read as if it were not

description: A field or method read from a value that may be `null`. `if let`, `??`, `?.` or a `!= null` check narrows it.
printed:
error[T04]: `user.email` may be null, so `.toUpperCase()` may fail
 --> src/App.wf:5:10

5 |     Text(user.email.toUpperCase())

fix: Unwrap it: `if let e = user.email { e.toUpperCase() }`, `user.email?.toUpperCase()`, or `(user.email ?? "").toUpperCase()`.

title: A secret where it would escape
plain: A secret where it would escape
summary: A `Secret` shown by an element, spliced into text, logged or kept with `persist`.
description: A `Secret` shown by an element, spliced into text, logged or kept with `persist`.

error[T12]: `token` is a `Secret`, and `Text` would show it
 --> src/App.wf:4:10

4 |     Text(token)
  |          ^^^^^

title: A name nothing declares
plain: A name nothing declares
summary: A name, or a function called, that no declaration, parameter, script or browser global provides — a ReferenceError the first time the page reads it.
description: A name, or a function called, that no declaration, parameter, script or browser global provides — a ReferenceError the first time the page reads it.
printed:
error[T13]: nothing declares `cuont`
 --> src/App.wf:4:30
  |
4 |     Button("+") { on click { cuont = count + 1 } }
  |                              ^^^^^
  = help: Did you mean `count`? Declare it — a `state`, a `const`, an `action`, a prop — or check the spelling. In the browser it would be a ReferenceError
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T13
fix:
Correct the spelling, or declare the name. The browser's own
globals (`window`, `navigator`, `Math` …) and the language's values
(`viewport`, `query`, `now` …) need no declaration; a call to a function
nothing declares — `uid()` for `uuid()` — is reported the same way. A
template rendered with data (`wf render`) reads its data's keys by name, so
it is not held to this.

title: A method a number, a string or a list does not have
plain: A method a number, a string or a list does not have
summary: In the browser the call is `x.method is not a function`, the first time the line runs. The message suggests the nearest method there is.
description: In the browser the call is `x.method is not a function`, the first time the line runs. The message suggests the nearest method there is.
printed:
error[T16]: a `[String]` has no method `joined`
 --> src/App.wf:4:16
  |
4 |     Text(names.joined(", "))
  |                ^^^^^^
  = help: Did you mean `join`?
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T16
fix: The method the message suggests — here `join`.

title: A comparison that is always the same
plain: A comparison that is always the same
summary: `==` or `!=` between values that can never be equal — a string and a number, a record and a string, an enum and a case it does not have — so the answer never changes.
description: `==` or `!=` between values that can never be equal — a string and a number, a record and a string, an enum and a case it does not have — so the…
printed:
error[T14]: `count` is `Number` and `"0"` is `String`, which are never equal, so this is always false
 --> src/App.wf:4:8
  |
4 |     if count == "0" { Text("Nothing yet") }
  |        ^^^^^
  = help: Convert one side: `Number(text) == n`, or `"{n}" == text`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T14
fix:
Compare values of one type: `count == 0`, or convert one side
(`Number(text) == n`). Against an enum, use a case it has.

title: An async result used before it is awaited
plain: An async result used before it is awaited
summary: An action that awaits hands back a promise; read as its result without `await` it is not one. `await` is written in an action, a handler, a timer or a hook — not in a `derived` value or an effect, which run at once — and `.pending` is for an action that awaits.
description: An action that awaits hands back a promise; read as its result without `await` it is not one. `await` is written in an action, a handler, a timer or…
printed:
error[T17]: `save` awaits nothing, so `.pending` is always false
 --> src/App.wf:5:30
  |
5 |     Button("Save", disabled: save.pending) { on click { save() } }
  |                              ^^^^
  = help: `.pending` is true while a call of an async action runs; an action that awaits nothing finishes before the page repaints
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T17
fix:
`.pending` is for an action that awaits — drop it here. An async
action's result is read with `await` inside an action or a handler; a value
that arrives over the network is a `resource`, which `derived` values and
elements can read.

title: A value that may be null, shown as text
plain: A value that may be null, shown as text
summary: Spliced into text, `null` shows as `null` (and a missing value as `undefined`). Say what to show instead with `??`.
description: Spliced into text, `null` shows as `null` (and a missing value as `undefined`). Say what to show instead with `??`.
printed:
warning[T19]: `user.nickname` may be null, and in text it would show as `null`
 --> src/App.wf:5:26
  |
5 |     Text("Also known as {user.nickname}")
  |                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Say what to show instead: `{user.nickname ?? ""}`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T19

fix:
Say what to show instead: `{user.nickname ?? "nothing yet"}`, or
show the line only when there is one: `if let n = user.nickname { … }`.

title: A list or a record shown as text
plain: A list or a record shown as text
summary: A list in text runs its items together with commas, and a map or a record shows as `[object Object]`. Show a field, or join a list of text.
description: A list in text runs its items together with commas, and a map or a record shows as `[object Object]`. Show a field, or join a list of text.
printed:
warning[T20]: `tags` is `[String]`, and in text it shows as its items run together with commas
 --> src/App.wf:4:19

4 |     Text("Tagged {tags}")
  |                   ^^^^
  = help: Show a field of it, or `.join(", ")` a list of text
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T20

title: Arithmetic on something that is not a number
plain: Arithmetic on something that is not a number
summary: `-`, `*`, `/` and `%` take numbers; on a string or a list the result is `NaN`. `+` joins text when one side is a string, and takes numbers otherwise.
description: `-`, `*`, `/` and `%` take numbers; on a string or a list the result is `NaN`. `+` joins text when one side is a string, and takes numbers otherwise.
printed:
error[T18]: `*` takes numbers, but `price` is `String`
 --> src/App.wf:3:27
  |
3 |     Heading("Total {price * 2}").h1
  |                           ^
  = help: Convert it: `Number(value)`; `+` joins text when one side is a string
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T18
fix:
Hold numbers as numbers (`state price = 12`), or convert:
`Number(price) * 2`.

title: A `match` that misses a case, or has one twice
plain: A match that misses a case, or has one twice
summary: A `match` with no `else` must give every case of the enum an arm — a value with a case it misses would match nothing. A case with two arms reaches only the first. A `match` expression that covers every case needs no `else`.
description: A `match` with no `else` must give every case of the enum an arm — a value with a case it misses would match nothing. A case with two arms reaches…
printed:
error[T15]: this `match` on `status` has no arm for `.review`, and no `else`
 --> src/App.wf:5:5
  |
5 |     match status {
  |     ^^^^^
  = help: Add an arm for each, or `else { … }` for the rest
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T15
fix:
Give every case its arm, or add `else { … }` for the rest. A
`match` expression that covers every case needs no `else`:
`derived label = match status { .draft { "Draft" } .review { "In review" } .live { "Live" } }`.

title: A handler that names more values than its event sends
plain: A handler that names more values than its event sends
summary: A handler names the values its event sends, in order: `on menu(key, x, y)` for a component's `event menu(key: String, x: Number, y: Number)`. A DOM event sends one value, the event itself. A name past the last value sent is never anything but `undefined`.
description: A handler names the values its event sends, in order: `on menu(key, x, y)` for a component's `event menu(key: String, x: Number, y: Number)`. A DOM…
printed:
error[T22]: `on menu` names 4 values, but `event menu(key: String, x: Number, y: Number)` sends 3 values
 --> src/App.wf:9:44
  |
9 |     Entry("notes.wf") { on menu(key, x, y, z) { at = "{key} at {x}, {y}" } }
  |                                            ^
  = help: Name at most 3, in order: `on menu(key, x, y)`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T22
why:
Error.

A handler names the values its event sends, in the order the event
declares them; it may name fewer, never more. A DOM event — `click`,
`input`, `keydown` — sends one value, the event itself, so `on click(e, x)`
is this error too.
fix:
Drop the extra names. For a DOM event, name the event alone and
read what it carries from it: `on click(e) { … e.clientX … }`.

title: A resource `match` with no `error` arm
plain: A resource match with no error arm
summary: When the request fails, a `match` with no `error` arm and no `else` shows nothing at all, and the reader is not told.
description: When the request fails, a `match` with no `error` arm and no `else` shows nothing at all, and the reader is not told.
printed:
warning[T21]: this `match` on `users` has no `error` arm, so a failed request shows nothing
 --> src/App.wf:4:5
  |
4 |     match users {
  |     ^^^^^
  = help: Add `error(e) { Alert(e.message).danger }`, or `else { … }`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/T21
why: Warning.
fix: `error(e) { Alert(e.message).danger }`, or an `else`.

title: A required prop or field left out
plain: A required prop or field left out
summary: A component's prop, or a record's field, that has no default is not given. The value would be `undefined` where the declaration promises one.
description: A component's prop, or a record's field, that has no default is not given. The value would be `undefined` where the declaration promises one.
printed:
error[C01]: `Todo(…)` leaves out `id` of `Todo`, which has no default
 --> src/App.wf:3:18
  |
3 |     state todo = Todo(title: "Write the docs")
  |                  ^^^^
  = help: Give it, or declare a default in the type: `field: Type = value`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/C01
fix:
Give it, or declare a default in the type (`id: String = ""`) or
on the prop.

A built-in that cannot be placed without a prop is held to it the same way:
a `Portal` with no `into:` would draw nowhere, and the fix passes
`into: null` for you to name the node.

title: A prop the component does not declare
plain: A prop the component does not declare
summary: Your own component is called with a prop it does not declare. Nothing in it reads the value, so the call does not do what it says; often a misspelling.
description: Your own component is called with a prop it does not declare. Nothing in it reads the value, so the call does not do what it says; often a misspelling.
printed:
error[C02]: `Badge2` declares no prop `colour`
 --> src/App.wf:4:19
  |
4 |     Badge2("New", colour: "red")
  |                   ^^^^^^
  = help: It is passed anyway, but nothing in the component reads it
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/C02
fix: Correct the spelling, or declare the prop on the component.

title: A part outside the component it belongs to
plain: A part outside the component it belongs to
summary: `Select.Option`, `Table.Row`, `Card.Header` — a part is placed inside its owner. Outside it, it draws a stray element with nothing around it.
description: `Select.Option`, `Table.Row`, `Card.Header` — a part is placed inside its owner. Outside it, it draws a stray element with nothing around it.
printed:
error[C03]: `Select.Option` is a part of `Select`, and it is not inside one
 --> src/App.wf:3:5
  |
3 |     Select.Option("Pro", value: "pro")
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Place it in a `Select { … }`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/C03
fix:
Place the part inside its owner: `Select(bind: plan) {
Select.Option(…) }`.

title: An attribute a built-in does not declare
plain: An attribute a built-in does not declare
summary: A named argument a built-in has no prop for is written to its element as an HTML attribute. `aria-*`, `data-*` and the global attributes are expected; anything else is usually a misspelling.
description: A named argument a built-in has no prop for is written to its element as an HTML attribute. `aria-*`, `data-*` and the global attributes are…
printed:
warning[C04]: Button has no prop `colour`; it is written to the element as an attribute
 --> src/App.wf:3:20
  |
3 |     Button("Save", colour: "red")
  |                    ^^^^^^
  = help: A typo here does nothing on screen; check the component's props
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/C04
why: Warning.
fix:
Check the prop's spelling — `wf registry` lists what the built-in
takes. `aria-*`, `data-*` and the global attributes (`id`, `role`,
`title`, …) are expected and draw nothing.

title: A positional argument a built-in does not take
plain: A positional argument a built-in does not take
summary: The built-in takes its arguments by name; one written without a name is not given to anything.
description: The built-in takes its arguments by name; one written without a name is not given to anything.
printed:
warning[C05]: Divider takes no positional argument
 --> src/App.wf:3:13
  |
3 |     Divider("thin")
  |             ^
  = help: Name it: the registry lists the props it takes
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/C05
why: Warning.
fix: Name it, with one of the props the built-in takes.

title: A positional argument bound by order
plain: A positional argument bound by order
summary: Your component declares no positional prop (`_ name`), so the argument is bound to its first prop. Mark that prop with `_` to say so.
description: Your component declares no positional prop (`_ name`), so the argument is bound to its first prop. Mark that prop with `_` to say so.
printed:
warning[C06]: `Tag2` declares no positional prop; the argument binds to `label`
 --> src/App.wf:4:10
  |
4 |     Tag2("new")
  |          ^
  = help: Mark the prop: `component Tag2(_ label: …)`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/C06
why: Warning.
fix: Mark the prop the call means: `component Tag2(_ label: String)`.

title: A drag or a gesture on a component with no one element
plain: A drag or a gesture on a component with no one element
summary: `drag:`, `dragGroup:`, `dropValue:`, `dropAxis:`, `dropInside:`, `on receive(d)`, `on dragmove(d)`, `on longpress` and `on swipe` written on your component's call belong to the one element it draws. A component whose body is an `if`, a `for`, a `show`, a `match` or several elements has none to give them, so wrap what it draws in one element, or write them inside it.
description: `drag:`, `dragGroup:`, `dropValue:`, `dropAxis:`, `dropInside:`, `on receive(d)`, `on dragmove(d)`, `on longpress` and `on swipe` written on your…
printed:
error[C07]: `drag:` on `Rows2` has no element to land on: its body is a `for`
 --> src/App.wf:6:16
  |
6 |     Rows2("a", drag: "a")
  |                ^^^^
  = help: Wrap what `Rows2` draws in one element (a `Stack`, a `Row`), or write `drag:` inside it
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/C07
why:
`drag:`, `dragGroup:`, `dropValue:`, `dropAxis:`, `dropInside:` and the
handlers of the gestures — `on receive(d)`, `on dragmove(d)`, `on
longpress`, `on swipe` — written on your component's call belong to the one
element it draws. A body that is an `if`, a `for`, a `show`, a `match` or
several elements has no one element to give them.
fix:
Wrap what the component draws in one element — a `Stack`, a `Row`
— or write the drag inside it, on the element it is for.

title: A route to nothing
plain: A route to nothing
summary: A link, a `navigate()` or a `Route` names a page or a path that no page has.
description: A link, a `navigate()` or a `Route` names a page or a path that no page has.
printed:
error[R01]: `/abuot` is not a route: no page's `path` matches it
 --> src/App.wf:3:5
  |
3 |     Link("About us", to: "/abuot")
  |     ^^^^
  = help: The nearest is `/about`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/R01
fix:
Link to a route a page has; the message names the nearest. A
spliced link is checked by its shape — `"/team/{t.slug}"` must match a route
like `/team/:slug` — a link with no leading `/` is refused (where it leads
would depend on the page it is on), and a link to a file (`/report.pdf`) or
another site is left alone.

title: A route parameter and a page parameter that do not match
plain: A route parameter and a page parameter that do not match
summary: A route's `:name` fills the page's parameter of that name; a `:name` with no parameter is read as nothing, and a parameter with no `:name` is never filled.
description: A route's `:name` fills the page's parameter of that name; a `:name` with no parameter is read as nothing, and a parameter with no `:name` is never filled.
printed:
error[R02]: the route `/u/:id` names `:id`, and the page declares no parameter `id`
 --> src/App.wf:1:1
  |
1 | page Profile(path: "/u/:id", title: "T", description: "D") {
  | ^^^^
  = help: Declare it: `page Profile(path: "/u/:id", id: String)`, then read `id`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/R02
fix:
Declare the parameter the route names — `page Profile(path:
"/u/:id", id: String)` — and read it by name; a declared parameter the route
has no `:name` for is never filled.

title: An `app` with no `Router`, or with two
plain: An app with no Router, or with two
summary: The current page is drawn where `app` places its `Router`. With none, no page is ever drawn; with two, the page has two places.
description: The current page is drawn where `app` places its `Router`. With none, no page is ever drawn; with two, the page has two places.
printed:
error[R03]: `app` places no `Router`, so no page is ever drawn
 --> src/App.wf:2:5
  |
2 |     Navbar { Navbar.Brand { Text("Ledger") } }

Place `Router` where the page belongs: `app { Navbar { … }
Router }`. (A program with no `app` at all routes its pages by itself.)

title: A relative URL on a nested route
plain: A relative URL on a nested route
summary: `"images/x.png"` is fetched relative to the page's address, so on `/blog/post` it is `/blog/images/x.png`. Written from the root, `"/images/x.png"`, it is the same file on every page.
description: `"images/x.png"` is fetched relative to the page's address, so on `/blog/post` it is `/blog/images/x.png`. Written from the root, `"/images/x.png"`,…

warning[R04]: `src: "images/cover.png"` is relative, so on `/blog/first` it is fetched from `/blog/images/cover.png`
 --> src/App.wf:3:5

  |     ^^^^^
  = help: Write it from the site's root: `"/images/cover.png"`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/R04
why: Warning.
fix: Write it from the site's root: `"/images/cover.png"`.

title: A translation of no page, or two in one language
plain: A translation of no page, or two in one language
summary: `translates:` names the page this one is a translation of, and the pages it joins list each other as `hreflang` alternates, each in its own `lang:`. A name no page has joins nothing, and two pages in one language would be two alternates for one `hreflang`.
description: `translates:` names the page this one is a translation of, and the pages it joins list each other as `hreflang` alternates, each in its own `lang:`.…
printed:
error[R05]: `HomeEn` translates `Hom`, and no page is named `Hom`
 --> src/App.wf:5:1
  |
5 | page HomeEn(path: "/en", title: "Home", description: "D", lang: "en", translates: Hom) {
  | ^^^^
  = help: Did you mean `Home`?
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/R05
why:
Error.

`translates:` names the page this one is a translation of, and the pages
it joins list each other as `hreflang` alternates, each in its own `lang:`.
Two pages of one group in the same language — or both with no `lang:`, so
both in the site's — would be two alternates for one language.
fix:
name a page the program declares, and give each translation the `lang:` it
is written in.

title: An assignment to something that cannot change
plain: An assignment to something that cannot change
summary: A `const`, a `derived` value, a prop, a route parameter, a loop variable or an action is assigned to. At run time the write throws, or changes a copy nothing reads.
description: A `const`, a `derived` value, a prop, a route parameter, a loop variable or an action is assigned to. At run time the write throws, or changes a copy…
printed:
error[X01]: `LIMIT` is a `const`, and nothing may assign to it
 --> src/App.wf:4:33
  |
4 |     Button("More") { on click { LIMIT = 4 } }
  |                                 ^^^^^
  = help: Declare it `state` if it changes; a constant is the same on every page
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/X01
fix:
Hold what changes in a `state`. A `derived` value changes when
what it reads does; a prop is its caller's (`emit` an event so the caller
changes it); a route parameter is the address's (`navigate`); a loop
variable is one pass's copy (change the item through its list).

title: An effect that feeds itself
plain: An effect that feeds itself
summary: An effect re-runs when what it reads changes. One that writes, every run, something it reads starts the next run itself: the page never settles, and the browser overflows its stack.
description: An effect re-runs when what it reads changes. One that writes, every run, something it reads starts the next run itself: the page never settles, and…
printed:
error[X02]: this effect writes `visits`, which it also reads, so each run starts the next and the page never settles
 --> src/App.wf:3:5
  |
3 |     effect { visits = visits + 1 }
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Work the value out with `derived` instead, or write it from the action that changes what it reads
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/X02
fix:
Work a value out with `derived`; change state from the action or
handler that changes what it depends on.

title: A derived value that changes something
plain: A derived value that changes something
summary: A `derived` value is worked out whenever what it reads changes, as often as the page needs it; one that calls an action that assigns changes state each time it is read.

printed:
error[X04]: `ticket` is worked out by calling `next(…)`, which assigns `count`
 --> src/App.wf:7:5
  |
7 |     derived ticket = next()
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: A derived value only reads; call the action from a handler, and derive from what it sets
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/X04
fix: Call the action from a handler; derive from the state it sets.

title: A state that copies a live value once
plain: A state that copies a live value once
summary: `now`, `viewport`, `query`, `hash`, `theme`, `network` and `update` keep themselves current, but a `state` takes its initial value once: `state clock = now(every: 1.seconds)` holds the moment the page opened, and everything worked out from it stays there. A `derived` value follows what it reads. A state the program goes on to assign or bind starts from the live value on purpose, and draws nothing.
description: `now`, `viewport`, `query`, `hash`, `theme`, `network` and `update` keep themselves current, but a `state` takes its initial value once: `state clock…
printed:
warning[X06]: `clock` copies `now` once, when the page opens, and never follows it
 --> src/App.wf:3:5
  |
3 |     state clock = now(every: 1.seconds)
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Nothing assigns `clock`: declare it `derived`, which is worked out again whenever `now` changes
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/X06
fix:
Declare it `derived` — the quick fix does. `derived clock =
now(every: 1.seconds)` is worked out again on every tick, and so is
everything that reads it. `now`, `viewport`, `query`, `hash`, `theme`,
`network` and `update` all keep themselves current; a `state` only takes
the value it starts with. A state the program assigns, binds or
changes in place is a starting value on purpose — `state tab = query.tab
?? "all"` that a click then changes — and draws nothing. Neither does a
live value read inside a lambda, which reads it each time it is called.

title: A `bind:` to something that cannot be written
plain: A bind: to something that cannot be written
summary: `bind:` writes what the control holds back to what it names: a state, a store's state, or a field of a loop's item. A constant, a derived value, a prop or a value worked out on the spot cannot take it.
description: `bind:` writes what the control holds back to what it names: a state, a store's state, or a field of a loop's item. A constant, a derived value, a…
printed:
error[F01]: `bind:` on `Input` writes back to what it names, and `name` is a `derived` value
 --> src/App.wf:5:11

5 |     Input(bind: name, label: "Name")
  |           ^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Bind a `state` (or a store's state, or a field of a loop's item); show a value with `value:`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/F01
fix:
Bind the state the reader edits (`bind: first`); show a value
that is worked out with `value:`.

title: A `bind:` to a state the control cannot hold

fix:
A number field is `Input(…).number`; a text field holds a

title: A `validate` block no control can satisfy
plain: A validate block no control can satisfy
summary: The rules of a `validate` block are shown on the control bound to the state, and a form is valid when they pass. On a state no control binds, or a derived value, they can never pass, and the submit stays disabled.
description: The rules of a `validate` block are shown on the control bound to the state, and a form is valid when they pass. On a state no control binds, or a…
printed:
error[F03]: `validate email` guards a state no control binds, so its rules can never be met
 --> src/App.wf:3:5

  = help: Bind it to the control the reader fills in: `Input(bind: email, …)`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/F03

Bind the state to the control the reader fills in:
`Input(bind: email, label: "Email").email`.

  = help: Start it as one of them (`free`, `pro`), so what is shown is what is held
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/F05

title: A file the project does not have
plain: A file the project does not have
summary: A site-relative `src:`, `poster:`, `captions:` or `transcript:` names a file that is not in `public/`; the page asks for it and gets nothing.
description: A site-relative `src:`, `poster:`, `captions:` or `transcript:` names a file that is not in `public/`; the page asks for it and gets nothing.
why:
Warning. `Image(src: "/img/hero.png")` when `public/img/hero.png` does not
exist (also a `Video`'s `poster:` and `captions:`, an `Audio`'s
`transcript:`, and a worker's `spawn("/workers/css.js")`): the page asks for it and gets a 404.
fix: put the file in `public/`, or correct the path.

title: A persisted value storage cannot keep
plain: A persisted value storage cannot keep
summary: `persist` writes its value to the browser's storage as JSON; a function, a file or a promise does not survive it.
description: `persist` writes its value to the browser's storage as JSON; a function, a file or a promise does not survive it.
printed:
error[D02]: `persist pick` keeps a function, which cannot be written to the browser's storage
 --> src/App.wf:2:5
  |
2 |     persist pick = (x) => x + 1
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Keep what it is made from — a name, an id, the data — and build it again when it is read
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/D02
fix:
Keep what it is made from — a name, an id, the data — and build
the rest when it is read.

title: A persisted value every instance shares
plain: A persisted value every instance shares
summary: A `persist` in a component placed more than once, or in a loop, is one stored value for all of them. `key:` gives each its own.
description: A `persist` in a component placed more than once, or in a loop, is one stored value for all of them. `key:` gives each its own.
printed:
warning[D03]: `persist open` is in `Panel`, which is placed more than once, so every one of them reads and writes one stored value
 --> src/App.wf:2:5
  |
2 |     persist open = false
  |     ^^^^^^^
  = help: Give each its own: `persist open = false { key: id }`, with `id` a prop that tells them apart
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/D03
why: Warning.
fix:
Give each instance its own key: `persist open = false { key: title
}`, with a prop that tells them apart.

title: A persisted shape changed with no new version
plain: A persisted shape changed with no new version
summary: What a returning reader's browser holds is the old shape; the page reads it as the new one. Raising `version:`, with a `migrate` step, brings it forward.
description: What a returning reader's browser holds is the old shape; the page reads it as the new one. Raising `version:`, with a `migrate` step, brings it forward.
why:
Warning. The build remembers what each `persist` held (in
`.wf-cache/persist.json`); when that changes — `persist items = []` becomes
`persist items = { open: [], done: [] }` — and `version:` does not, a
returning reader's browser hands the old shape to code written for the new
one.
fix:
raise `version:` and add `migrate 1 -> 2 { … }` to bring the
old value forward.

title: An asset from another origin with no integrity hash
plain: An asset from another origin with no integrity hash
summary: A stylesheet, font or script loaded from another origin is code that origin can change after you read it. A `meta.integrity` hash is how the browser checks it has not.
description: A stylesheet, font or script loaded from another origin is code that origin can change after you read it. A `meta.integrity` hash is how the browser…
why:
Warning. A font, stylesheet or script in `meta.fonts`, `meta.stylesheets`
or `meta.scripts` from another origin, with no hash in `meta.integrity`.
fix:
add its `sha384-…` hash to `meta.integrity` (the CDN usually
publishes it). Google Fonts is exempt: its stylesheet differs per browser.

title: A message no translation has
plain: A message no translation has
summary: `t("key")` names a key no locale's file holds, so the page shows the key itself.
description: `t("key")` names a key no locale's file holds, so the page shows the key itself.
why:
`t("nav.blgo")` when no locale's file holds `nav.blgo`: the page shows
`nav.blgo`.
fix: the key the message suggests, or add it to the files.

title: A message and its call that disagree
plain: A message and its call that disagree
summary: The call passes a value the message does not use, or the message shows a placeholder the call does not pass, which then shows as written.
description: The call passes a value the message does not use, or the message shows a placeholder the call does not pass, which then shows as written.
why:
`t("greeting", { nme: user.name })` against `"greeting": "Hello, {name}!"`:
`nme` is not used, and `{name}` shows as written.
fix:
pass what the
message shows, by the name it shows it.

title: A message one locale has and another does not
plain: A message one locale has and another does not
summary: A reader in the locale that lacks it sees the key instead of the words.
description: A reader in the locale that lacks it sees the key instead of the words.
why:
Warning. `nav.blog` in `en.json` and not in `ar.json`: a reader in Arabic
sees `nav.blog`.
fix: translate it, or remove it from the others.

title: A locale the project does not have
plain: A locale the project does not have
summary: `setLocale("xx")` names a locale `i18n.locales` does not list.
description: `setLocale("xx")` names a locale `i18n.locales` does not list.
why: `setLocale("fr")` when `i18n.locales` is `["en", "ar"]`.
fix:
add the
locale and its file, or name one that exists.

title: Words a reader sees that are not translated
plain: Words a reader sees that are not translated
summary: Under `i18n.literals`, text that splices more than a name, or a value shown by a name that does not say it is words, is never looked up: every reader sees it as written.
description: Under `i18n.literals`, text that splices more than a name, or a value shown by a name that does not say it is words, is never looked up: every reader…
why:
Warning, under `"literals": true`. `Text("{plural(n, "file")} found")`
splices a call, so no table can key it; `derived said = "{n} errors"`
shown as `Text(said)` is not looked up, because only a value whose name
says it is words (`saidText`, `errorsLabel`) is. A reader in Arabic sees
both in English.
fix:
splice names, `derived filesText = "{n} files"`
then `Text("{filesText} found")`, and name what is words as words.

title: An allow that allows nothing
plain: An allow that allows nothing
summary: A `// wf-allow(CODE)` comment covers the next line of code (or its own, at the end of one); when nothing it names is reported there, or it names an error no allow may silence, it is reported itself — so allows cannot outlive what they were written for.
description: A `// wf-allow(CODE)` comment covers the next line of code (or its own, at the end of one); when nothing it names is reported there, or it names an…
printed:
warning[U07]: `wf-allow(U01)` allows nothing: no `U01` is reported on the line it covers
 --> src/App.wf:2:5
  |
2 |     // wf-allow(U01)
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Remove it — what it was written for is gone
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/U07
why:
A `// wf-allow(CODE)` comment accepts one finding on purpose: on a line of
its own it covers the next line of code, and at the end of a line it covers
that line. It names codes (`U01`) or families (`U`), comma-separated, and
only what `lints` could lower — a warning, or an error that ships no broken
page. An allow that covers nothing it names is reported, so allows cannot
outlive what they were written for.
fix: Remove the allow — what it was written for is gone.

title: Markup put in as markup
plain: Markup put in as markup
summary: An `Unsafe.Html`, and whether what it puts in went through `sanitize`; and a `Frame(srcdoc:)` drawing HTML from a value, which is sandboxed (`sandbox=""`) unless it says what it may do.
description: An `Unsafe.Html`, and whether what it puts in went through `sanitize`; and a `Frame(srcdoc:)` drawing HTML from a value, which is sandboxed…
printed:
warning[V03]: `Unsafe.Html` puts markup in as markup
 --> src/App.wf:4:5

  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Anything the project did not write itself belongs in `sanitize(…)` first
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/V03
fix:
Most text wants no markup of its own: write it as Markdown, which `Markdown(body)` draws with any HTML in it shown as text. Markup that must stay markup and comes from outside the project goes through `sanitize(…)` first — `Unsafe.Html(sanitize(body))` — which is the reviewed case, and the warning still names it. A `Frame(srcdoc:)` drawing HTML from a value is named too: that HTML is a document of its own, scripts and all. Unless the call says what the frame may do, it may do nothing — the build gives it `sandbox=""` — and the warning says so. Writing `sandbox:` out is the reviewed case; `allow-scripts` with `allow-same-origin` undoes the sandbox, and is named again. ```wf expect=V03 page P(path: "/", title: "T", description: "D") { state html = "

Hi

title: A long list that is not windowed
plain: A long list that is not windowed
summary: A `VirtualList` draws only the rows in view of one keyed `for` — `for row in rows by row.id { … }` — that is the whole of its body; with anything else in it, or a `for` with no `by`, it draws everything, as a plain scrolling box does.
description: A `VirtualList` draws only the rows in view of one keyed `for` — `for row in rows by row.id { … }` — that is the whole of its body; with anything…
printed:
warning[V12]: This `VirtualList` draws every row: its body is not one keyed `for`
 --> src/App.wf:4:5
  |
4 |     VirtualList(rowHeight: 32) {
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Make its body one `for` with a `by`: `VirtualList(rowHeight: 32) { for row in rows by row.id { … } }`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/V12
why:
A `VirtualList` draws only the rows in view of the one keyed `for` that is
the whole of its body. With anything else beside the `for`, or a `for` with
no `by` — which has no way to keep a row's nodes as it scrolls — it draws
every row, as a plain scrolling box does, and the length of the list is
what the page pays for.
fix:
Give the `for` a `by`, and move anything else — a heading, a
count — outside the `VirtualList`.

  |          ^^^

why:
A `Host` is made of one of a few elements: `div`, `span`, `canvas`, `svg`,
`section`, `figure`, `pre`, `p`, `ul` or `table` — the tag is written into
the document, so it is an allow-list rather than whatever the string says.
Any other tag is a `div`.
fix:
Make it one of the tags `Host` makes, or use the element the
built-ins offer for it (`Video`, `Audio`, `Image`).

why:
A call of a built-in's name draws the built-in, so a component declared
with that name is never drawn: its body, its props, its slots go unused, and
what the page shows is the built-in instead. It happens to a component
written before WebFluent gained an element of the same name — a `Footer`
from WebFluent 2, a `Chart` from before 5.2.
fix: Rename the component and its call sites.
